result.title: When Links Mislead: Label-Free Structural Polarity for Zero-Shot Classification of Web Pages
result.summary: Web platforms such as digital libraries, online stores and university sites must classify new pages before anyone labels them. Large language models (LLMs) can label each page from its text, but these labels are noisy, and links could correct them only where linked pages share classes. Existing zero-shot methods ignore the links, or pull a page toward its neighbours as label propagation and graph neural networks (GNNs) do, which hurts where linked pages differ in class. Others weight propagation by an LLM-estimated homophily that costs extra calls and drifts across LLMs. We find that the sign with which links should enter a prediction, which we call structural polarity, is readable without true labels. It is the excess agreement of LLM labels and text-prototype predictions along links. We thus propose ZeroPolar, which gates one signed propagation step by this statistic. Training-free ZeroPolar mixes prototype scores with any number of LLM labels, and ZeroPolar-T denoises the labels with a text classifier once half of the pages carry one. With one GPT-4o label per page, ZeroPolar-T reaches the highest mean accuracy on eleven graphs (73.99%), 6.01 points above LLM-BP and significantly above all eighteen baselines we compare. With LLM labels on only 5% of the pages, training-free ZeroPolar leads a GNN trained on these labels by 10.80 points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究零样本网页分类中链接结构可能误导的问题，提出用 LLM 标签与文本原型预测沿链接的「超额一致」无标签地估计结构极性，并据此门控一次带符号传播（ZeroPolar），以及在部分页面已有标注后用文本分类器去噪（ZeroPolar-T）。
AI.relevance_reason: 任务本身不涉及视觉推理，但其「用无需真值的统计量判断外部结构证据应当正向还是反向注入，并门控单步传播」的做法，可能为 LVR 中判定视觉证据与语言先验是否一致、何时抑制旁路信息的门控设计提供核查线索。
